text: In twenty ten, a new phone had a strange problem.
asr: In 2010, a new phone had a strange problem.

text: Hold it by the bottom corner, and the signal dropped.
Why? The metal edge in your hand is the antenna.
From the chip, a thin cable carries the signal to the frame.
The ring is cut: each plastic slit splits off a separate antenna.
Each piece is sized to its band.
Seven hundred megahertz needs about eleven centimetres. Three point five gigahertz, just two.
asr: 700 megahertz needs about 11 centimetres, 3.5 gigahertz just 2.

text: Now grip the corner. Your hand bridges the slit, and the signal fades.
So phones learned to switch to the antenna your hand isn't covering.
You're not holding it wrong. You are holding the antenna.
